LESSON: READING 13.4.1 SHORT STORY: STYLE (CLASS READER)

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.4: Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader), part of Strand 13 in Grade 8 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How does a writer make a story interesting? 2. Which qualities of a person can be given to animals?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify personification and flashback in a short story,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the creative use of language in short stories.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify personification and flashback in a short story,

   Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. read and dramatise selected parts of a short story featuring personification and flashback,

   Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the creative use of language in short stories.

   Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read in turns the selected short story,

2. narrate the sequence of events in the selected short story,

3. identify personification and flashback in the selected short story,

4. dramatise in groups the selected parts of the story containing personification and flashback,

5. make short notes on personification and flashback with examples from the short story. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read in turns the selected short story,
2. narrate the sequence of events in the selected short story,
3. identify personification and flashback in the selected short story,
4. dramatise in groups the selected parts of the story containing personification and flashback,
5. make short notes on personification and flashback with examples from the short story. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 13.4.1 Short Story: Style (Class Reader) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn: It is enhanced as the learner works collaboratively to dramatise selected parts of the story.

Values:
Responsibility: It is promoted as the learner takes up tasks assigned to them as they dramatise the story.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Decision making skills: They are enhanced as the learner identifies instances of personification and flashback.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Stylistic devices such as personification and flashback are relevant in the creation scripts in Creative arts and sports.
